title: GCD: DispatchGroup & Concurrent Queues
hints: `group.enter()` before dispatching, `group.leave()` when the work finishes.
Append results through a serial queue so concurrent writes don't race.
`group.wait()` then sort — completion order isn't deterministic.
jsBridge: `DispatchGroup` with `enter`/`leave`/`wait` is pre-async fan-out/fan-in, like hand-counting outstanding callbacks before `Promise.all` existed. Task groups replace it in modern Swift.

compass.q: Before `Promise.all`, JS devs counted callbacks with a counter. How is `DispatchGroup` the same idea?
Forgetting a `leave()` or calling it twice: what happens?
`group.wait()` (blocks the thread) vs `group.notify(queue:)` vs `withTaskGroup`: which never blocks?
Where does `DispatchGroup` still appear: legacy code, `XCTestExpectation`-style waiting?
